ports.name: clk_i

signals.name: pmpcfg
signals.functionality: Holds 8-bit PMP configuration per region written from CSR write data when enabled and not locked. Its bits are read back (cfg_rd) and used by matching and permission logic.
signals.evidence: csr_pmpcfg process captures ctrl_i.csr_wdata into pmpcfg(i); pmpcfg used by perm_gen, match_gen and pmpaddr write conditions

signals.name: pmpcfg_we
signals.functionality: Combines CSR address and write-enable to produce per-byte write enables for pmpcfg; these strobes gate updates of pmpcfg registers.
signals.evidence: csr_we_cfg process sets pmpcfg_we(...) based on ctrl_i.csr_addr and ctrl_i.csr_we; csr_pmpcfg checks pmpcfg_we(i/4) = '1'

signals.name: pmpaddr
signals.functionality: Stores PMP region addresses written from CSR data when enabled and not locked. Used for readback and for computing comparisons (cmp_ge, cmp_lt) used in matching.
signals.evidence: csr_pmpaddr process writes pmpaddr(i) <= "00" & ctrl_i.csr_wdata(...); addr_read_back and cmp generation read pmpaddr

signals.name: pmpaddr_we
signals.functionality: Generated from CSR address and write-enable bits to select which pmpaddr element is written; these strobes gate pmpaddr writes in the clocked process.
signals.evidence: csr_we_addr process sets pmpaddr_we(...) based on ctrl_i.csr_addr and ctrl_i.csr_we; csr_pmpaddr checks pmpaddr_we(i) = '1'

signals.name: cfg_rd
signals.functionality: Reflects stored pmpcfg bytes for readback; each cfg_rd(i) is assigned directly from pmpcfg(i) and then used to form 32-bit cfg_rd32 words.
signals.evidence: cfg_rd(i) <= pmpcfg(i) in csr_read_back_gen; cfg_rd32 built from cfg_rd entries

signals.name: cfg_rd32
signals.functionality: Aggregates four cfg_rd bytes into XLEN-bit words for CSR readback. These words feed csr_o during CSR read access.
role: aggregates cfg bytes for CSR read
signals.evidence: cfg_rd32(i) <= cfg_rd(i*4+3) & cfg_rd(i*4+2) & cfg_rd(i*4+1) & cfg_rd(i*4+0); csr_read_access assigns csr_o <= cfg_rd32(...)

signals.name: addr_rd
signals.functionality: Provides readback of PMP addresses with certain low-bit adjustments; it is assigned from slices of pmpaddr and conditional low-bit overrides depending on granularity and TOR/NAP settings.
signals.evidence: address_read_back process assigns addr_rd(i)(XLEN-3 downto pmp_lsb_c-2) <= pmpaddr(i)(XLEN-3 downto pmp_lsb_c-2) and conditionally sets low bits

signals.name: acc_addr
signals.functionality: Selects between the CPU next PC or the LSU address depending on lsu_mo_we and supplies the address used by comparison and matching logic.
signals.evidence: acc_addr <= ctrl_i.pc_nxt when (ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '0') else addr_ls_i; comparisons use acc_addr(...) in cmp_na/cmp_ge/cmp_lt

signals.name: acc_priv
signals.functionality: Selects between CPU privilege or LSU privilege depending on lsu_mo_we and supplies the privilege used by permission logic (perm_gen) and initial fail condition.
signals.evidence: acc_priv <= ctrl_i.cpu_priv when (ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we = '0') else ctrl_i.lsu_priv; perm_gen reads acc_priv

signals.name: addr_mask_napot
signals.functionality: Combinationally builds per-region masks for NAPOT matching from pmpaddr bits. These masks feed addr_mask when NAP mode is enabled.
signals.evidence: addr_mask_napot bits computed in nap_mode_enable generates using pmpaddr(r)(i-3) in generate loops

signals.name: addr_mask
signals.functionality: Captured on clock from addr_mask_napot when the region is in NAPOT mode (cfg_al_c = '1'), otherwise set to all ones. Used by cmp_na and by readback adjustments.
signals.evidence: addr_masking process: on rising_edge(clk_i) if pmpcfg(r)(cfg_al_c) = '1' then addr_mask(r) <= addr_mask_napot(r) else addr_mask(r) <= (others => '1')

signals.name: cmp_na
signals.functionality: Per-region combinational comparison that checks masked acc_addr equality with masked pmpaddr to indicate NAPOT matches when NAP_EN is enabled.
signals.evidence: cmp_na(r) <= '1' when ((acc_addr(...) and addr_mask(r)) = (pmpaddr(r)(...) and addr_mask(r))) and NAP_EN else '0'

signals.name: cmp_ge
signals.functionality: Per-region combinational comparisons that indicate acc_addr >= previous region address (or '1' for region 0) when TOR is enabled; used by match logic for TOR mode.
signals.evidence: cmp_ge defined in addr_match_r0_gen and addr_match_rn_gen using comparisons against pmpaddr(...) when TOR_EN

signals.name: cmp_lt
signals.functionality: Per-region combinational comparisons that indicate acc_addr < region address for regions >0 when TOR is enabled; used by match logic for TOR mode.
signals.evidence: cmp_lt defined in addr_match_rn_gen using unsigned(acc_addr(...)) < unsigned(pmpaddr(...)) when TOR_EN

signals.name: match
signals.functionality: Computed combinationally from pmpcfg mode bits and the cmp_ge/cmp_lt/cmp_na comparisons to indicate whether the access matches a region under TOR or NAPOT modes.
signals.evidence: match_gen process assigns match(r) from pmpcfg(...)=mode_tor_c and cmp_ge/cmp_lt or from cmp_na when NAP_EN

signals.name: allow
signals.functionality: Combinational per-region outputs from permission logic (perm_gen) that indicate whether the requested access type is allowed given pmpcfg bits and acc_priv. It is the source for fault accumulation.
signals.evidence: perm_gen process assigns allow(r) based on ctrl_i.lsu_mo_we, ctrl_i.lsu_rw, acc_priv and pmpcfg bits

signals.name: fail
signals.functionality: Combinational vector forming a priority chain: fail(NUM_REGIONS) reflects acc_priv != M mode, and each lower index is set to not allow(r) when match(r) is asserted, otherwise passes fail(r+1). fail(0) is used to set fault_o.
signals.evidence: fail(NUM_REGIONS) <= '1' when (acc_priv /= priv_mode_m_c) else '0'; fail(r) <= not allow(r) when (match(r) = '1') else fail(r+1); fault_check uses fail(0)
